title: fix(web): give each mock API request a connection of its own in the tests (#206)
body:
## Summary Under load, the web tests' mocked chat `fetch` sometimes failed with Undici's `SocketError: closed`. The cause, traced with temporary socket logging on Node 26.9.0, which bundles Undici 8.10.2: 1. MSW answers `fetch` at the socket level, so Undici's keep-alive pool holds the mock's connections. 2. After the unmount test aborts its chat request mid-stream, Undici reopens that connection and writes nothing to it. 3. `@mswjs/interceptors` passes a connection that is read from but not written to within one `setImmediate` through to the real network, where nothing listens at `localhost:3000`. 4. Under load, the scroll test's chat request goes out on that connection before the refusal comes back, and it fails. The cause is in third-party code, so this is a mitigation in the test transport (r1/Q-1). `src/test/setup.ts` installs `connectionPerRequest` from `src/mocks/node.ts`. It is an `undici` dispatcher that gives each request a client of its own and closes it after that request. Nothing retries, and no wait or timeout changed. The full write-up, with each decision and the alternative it beat, is in [the journal entry](docs/journal/2026-10-07-the-closed-socket-was-a-passthrough.md). Closes #206 **PRD requirements:** none (test infrastructure) **ADRs:** none ## Verification - [x] `npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm test`: pass at `07b1c20` (the head, `1290e3a`, adds one journal sentence, and `npm run lint` passes on it), 2908 tests passed and 3 skipped in 118 files (the DynamoDB turn-store file's reachability probe skipped its 3 tests in that run, with DynamoDB Local up). - [x] `npm run test:coverage && npm run coverage:changed`: 2911 of 2911 tests, and "every added source line since origin/main ran in a test". `npm run dup:changed` (report-only) reports one clone: `ChatPage.errors.test.tsx:450-457` copies `useChat.test.tsx:62-70` (8 lines), the hoisted api in two tests. Nick's decision on the review accepts it. - [x] Seen failing (Node 26.9.0): `npm run --silent mutate -- edits.json --markdown -- npx vitest run apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts`. CI's check covers `node.ts`. `setup.ts` is in a `test/` directory, which CI skips, but it gets a row too, per the definition of done (A-5). | Edit | File | Change | Status | Failed tests | |---|---|---|---|---| | setup-dispatcher | `apps/web/src/test/setup.ts` | ` setGlobalDispatcher(connectionPerRequest);⏎` → `` | KILLED | `apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts > the test transport (#206) sends each mock API request over a connection of its own`
`apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts > the test transport (#206) keeps a request on the mock when the connection Undici reopened after an aborted request fails (forces the failure on Node 26's Undici 8.10)`
`apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts > the test transport (#206) closes each connection once its response has ended` | | client-per-request | `apps/web/src/mocks/node.ts` | ` const client = new Client(String(options.origin));⏎ const accepted = client.dispatch(options, handler);⏎ void client.close();⏎ return accepted;⏎` → ` const pooled = ((globalThis as { pooled206?: Map }).pooled206 ??= new Map());⏎ const client = pooled.get(String(options.origin)) ?? new Client(String(options.origin));⏎ pooled.set(String(options.origin), client);⏎ return client.dispatch(options, handler);⏎` | KILLED | `apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts > the test transport (#206) sends each mock API request over a connection of its own`
`apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts > the test transport (#206) closes each connection once its response has ended` | | close-after-request | `apps/web/src/mocks/node.ts` | ` void client.close();⏎` → `` | KILLED | `apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts > the test transport (#206) closes each connection once its response has ended` | 3 edits: 3 killed, 0 killed other tests, 0 survived, 0 timed out, 0 errors, 0 refused - [x] Seen failing (Node 26.9.0), `testUtils.ts`: its only change is a header line (see "Shared-file or contract changes"), so its row shows instead that `node.test.ts`'s new `until` wait is what the close test relies on: `npm run --silent mutate -- edits-until.json --markdown -- npx vitest run apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts`. | Edit | File | Change | Status | Failed tests | |---|---|---|---|---| | until-no-wait | `apps/web/src/chat/testUtils.ts` | ` if (condition()) return;⏎` → ` return;⏎` | KILLED | `apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts > the test transport (#206) closes each connection once its response has ended` | 1 edits: 1 killed, 0 killed other tests, 0 survived, 0 timed out, 0 errors, 0 refused - [x] Seen failing (Node 26.9.0), the hoisted api in the two `.errors` tests: `npm run --silent mutate -- edits-hoist.json --markdown -- npx vitest run apps/web/src/chat/ChatPage.errors.test.tsx`. Putting `createChatApi()` back inside the render callback makes each test loop until it times out. | Edit | File | Change | Status | Failed tests | |---|---|---|---|---| | hoist-retry-twice | `apps/web/src/chat/ChatPage.errors.test.tsx` | ` configureMockApi({ chatFault: "network" });⏎ // One api for every render (#206): a new one reruns the session effect, which then loops.⏎ const api = createChatApi();⏎ const { result } = renderHook(() => useChat(api, { reducedMotion: instant }));⏎` → ` configureMockApi({ chatFault: "network" });⏎ const { result } = renderHook(() => useChat(createChatApi(), { reducedMotion: instant }));⏎` | KILLED | `apps/web/src/chat/ChatPage.errors.test.tsx > ChatPage: Retry (FR-015) runs one retry when Retry is called twice before re-rendering`
`apps/web/src/chat/ChatPage.errors.test.tsx > ChatPage: Retry (FR-015) keeps Retry keyboard-operable: Enter on the focused button retries` | | hoist-no-error | `apps/web/src/chat/ChatPage.errors.test.tsx` | ` it("does nothing on Retry when there is no error", async () => {⏎ // One api for every render (#206): a new one reruns the session effect, which then loops.⏎ const api = createChatApi();⏎ const { result } = renderHook(() => useChat(api, { reducedMotion: instant }));⏎` → ` it("does nothing on Retry when there is no error", async () => {⏎ const { result } = renderHook(() => useChat(createChatApi(), { reducedMotion: instant }));⏎` | KILLED | `apps/web/src/chat/ChatPage.errors.test.tsx > ChatPage: Retry (FR-015) does nothing on Retry when there is no error` | 2 edits: 2 killed, 0 killed other tests, 0 survived, 0 timed out, 0 errors, 0 refused - [x] Checked by hand only, with no test: - the before/after load rounds and the 36-way reproduction below, which are measurements, not tests; - that the web suite passes on Node 24.21.0 as well as on Node 26.9.0 (439 of 439 on each). CI runs Node 24. - that undici's `new Agent({ pipelining: 0 })` in place of `connectionPerRequest` also passes `node.test.ts` on Node 24.21.0 and 26.9.0 (run once, then reverted; see "Decisions the spec left open"). - [ ] Eval smoke suite: not applicable, since the agent, prompts, tools and model config are unchanged. - [ ] `sam validate`: not applicable, since there are no infra changes. ### AC1: the reproduction (r1/Q-2) `apps/web/src/mocks/node.test.ts`, with the fix reverted (the `setup-dispatcher` row) and with it in place. The Node 24 column was re-run at `07b1c20`, the review round's head (mutate with `npx -y node@24`): | Test | Node 26.9.0, no fix → fix | Node 24.21.0, no fix → fix | |---|---|---| | keeps a request on the mock when the connection Undici reopened after an aborted request fails (forces the failure on Node 26's Undici 8.10) | red (`fetch failed`, `ECONNRESET`) → green | green → green | | sends each mock API request over a connection of its own (the mechanism the fix changes) | red → green | red → green | | closes each connection once its response has ended | red → green | red → green | The forced test points a kept-alive connection at a real local server's origin and aborts a request on it mid-response. The server receives the passed-through connection and resets it while the next request waits in its mock handler. The server stands in for the refusal at `localhost:3000`, whose timing a test can't control. On Node 24 (Undici 7), the reopened connection is destroyed (`ClientDestroyedError`) before any request uses it, so the forced test can't go red there. The mechanism test is the one that does, on both versions; Q-2 allows this. What the reproduction shows as the cause is the request sent over a connection that was passed through and then failed. That Undici's reconnect after the abort is the only route to such a connection is suspected, not shown. ### AC3: load rounds Each round ran six full `npx vitest run` suites in parallel from the repo root, without coverage, with the temporary `fetch` logging (each rejected `fetch` and its `cause`) injected into `setup.ts` and removed afterwards. There were three rounds before at `6d1e593` and three after at `f86d357`, back to back on one 8-core machine. The web code at `66c0981`, the base, is the same as at `6d1e593`. DynamoDB Local (`sched-dynamodb-local`) was up for every round. Under load its reachability probe still skipped some DynamoDB tests: in 17 of 18 before suites and 14 of 15 after suites. That applies to both sides alike. Load average (median / max per round): before 139/197, 260/489, 151/232; after 303/419, 134/182, 91/153. **Killed suites.** - Two first attempts at a round, before 1 and after 2, died partway as a whole and were rerun. - From after round 2 onwards, each suite ran in its own session (`setsid`). After that only single suites died (`Killed: 9`): 3 of the 18 after suites. Their `fetch` logs show no `SocketError` either. - So the counts compare 18 complete suites before with 15 after. - Suspected, not verified: `scripts/mutate.test.ts` "kills a timed-out command's whole process group…" (it failed in 1 before and 3 after suites) reached the wrong process group under load. "Own" means the test's own wait, timeout or assertion. "Knock-on" means it failed after an earlier test in its file timed out. | Test | Before (18 suites), own / knock-on | After (15 suites), own / knock-on | |---|---|---| | `ChatPage.test.tsx` scroll test | 3 / 0 (see below) | **0 / 0** | | `ChatPage.errors.test.tsx` "…stream whose last line is cut mid-way" | 0 / 0 | **0 / 0** | | `VoiceInput.test.tsx` "the mic button (FR-020) opens the overlay…" | 2 / 0 | 0 / 0 | | `src/auth/session.test.ts` "uses the Cognito mock in development…" (known failure under load, A-2) | 18 / 0 | 15 / 0 | | `src/auth/session.test.ts` "uses the IDs baked into the build" | 0 / 14 | 0 / 13 | | `src/auth/session.test.ts` "is one service, and getIdToken reads its session" | 0 / 8 | 0 / 4 | | `fetch` rejections with `SocketError: closed` (from the logging) | **1** (scroll test) | **0** | No other web test failed in any round. The scroll test's 3 before-failures: - one at the chip step (`:548`) with the logged `SocketError: closed`; - one at the chip step with no rejected `fetch` logged; - one at the last step (`:558`) with no rejected `fetch` logged. The last two have no identified cause. Tests outside `apps/web` that failed in any round, before → after, own/knock-on. All are timing or DynamoDB-probe failures under load, and this PR doesn't touch them: - `packages/evals`: - `suite.test.ts` "computes pass@1…" 18/0 → 15/0, with its four knock-ons 0/18 → 0/15 and "an errored trial…" 0/16 → 0/13; - `l1.test.ts` "forbid_tools…" 18/0 → 15/0; - `graders.test.ts` "end_state appointment…" 18/0 → 13/2; - `calibration.test.ts` "exports 20 by default…" 18/0 → 6/9 and "exports pass/fail trials…" 0/0 → 9/0; - `judge-wiring.test.ts` "records the judge's rejected replies…" 8/5 → 8/7 and "the budget guard counts the judge's spend" 5/13 → 0/15; - smaller counts in `graders`, `judge-wiring`, `l1`, `runner` and `simulator`. - `packages/tools`: - `in-memory.test.ts` "snapshot()…" 4/0 → 3/0; - `dynamo.test.ts` (DynamoDB Local): 0–12 own per failing test before, 0–11 after (failures under load). - `services/api`: - `session.local.test.ts` file failure 7 → 6; - `dynamo-turn-store.local.test.ts` 1–2 → 3–4 own per test. - `scripts`: - `seed-data.test.ts` 16/0 → 11/0; - `mutate.test.ts` 3+1+0 → 3+3+1 own across three tests; - `coverage-changed.test.ts` 1/0 → 1/0. The full per-test table is in the agent's scratch output and can be reproduced with the commands above. **36-way reproduction** (`ChatPage.test.tsx` in 36 parallel runs): - Before, on the branch base: 7 of 36 failed, then 12 of 36. Every failure was the scroll test with `SocketError: closed`, and each had a socket destroyed from the interceptor's `#onRealSocketError`. - After, on the branch: 36 of 36 passed. There was no `SocketError` and no passed-through socket. The load average was 49 at the end of the run. ## Shared-file or contract changes - `apps/web/package.json` and `package-lock.json`: `undici@^8.11.2` added as an `apps/web` devDependency. r1/Q-1 allowed this, and open issue #29 also owns these files. undici 8.11.2 was already in the lockfile, hoisted for jsdom. - `apps/web/src/chat/useChat.test.tsx` (2 tests) and `apps/web/src/chat/ChatPage.errors.test.tsx` (2 tests): `createChatApi()` hoisted into a `const` out of `renderHook`'s render callback, with a comment, as Nick's [decision](https://github.com/nick-delgado/serverless-ai-scheduling/issues/206#issuecomment-6046867027) on the issue says. The `.errors` tests first passed it as `initialProps` instead, to avoid a `dup:changed` clone; the review flagged that, and Nick chose the hoist there too ([decision](https://github.com/nick-delgado/serverless-ai-scheduling/pull/214#issuecomment-6049709465)). A new api on every render reruns `useChat`'s session effect, and once session requests succeed, it loops until the test times out: 43,757 requests in one test. Before the fix, those session requests were aborted or failed on a passed-through connection, so the loop never started. - `apps/web/src/chat/testUtils.ts` (outside the owned paths, one header line): its list of test files that wait with `until` and keep the default timeout now names `mocks/node.test.ts`, which waits with `until` since the review round. CLAUDE.md asks for a list a change makes incomplete to be fixed in the same PR. - `apps/web/README.md`: the "Tests" bullet now says `setup.ts` gives `fetch` a connection per request (A-8). - `docs/journal/2026-10-06-…md`: its "What's next" #206 bullet now links the new entry (A-8). ## Decisions the spec left open See "Why we chose what we chose" in [the journal entry](docs/journal/2026-10-07-the-closed-socket-was-a-passthrough.md). It covers: - one connection per request rather than a narrower undici fix; - the reproduction's real local server standing in for a refusal; - the Node 24 limit of the forced test, which its title now states; - keeping the `ConnectionPerRequest` class rather than undici's `new Agent({ pipelining: 0 })`, which also passes `node.test.ts`; the class's header gives the reason, labelled untested (Nick's [decision](https://github.com/nick-delgado/serverless-ai-scheduling/pull/214#issuecomment-6049709465)). ## Docs - [ ] ADR: none needed, since this is a test-only transport change. - [x] Journal entry: `docs/journal/2026-10-07-the-closed-socket-was-a-passthrough.md`, with its index row. - [ ] PRD: no change. ## Deferred / follow-ups - Unexplained: a keep-alive `new Agent()` from the undici 8.11.2 package also passes the forced test, but Node 26's bundled Undici 8.10.2 doesn't. We didn't find which change accounts for that. - Suspected: `scripts/mutate.test.ts` SIGKILLs a process group outside its own under load. Worth an issue if load rounds are used again. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01E9XgjhqxuFbLZgmmAx6g66
